Gemini’s VPN Workaround Stops Working for Some Users in Russia
Evidence: VPN access, algorithmic profiling, geo-blocking
#Aletheia #Tech

Google's Gemini AI stopped working for some users in Russia via VPN workarounds, coinciding with the rollout of Gemini 3.7 Flash and stricter behavioral tracking.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +1.00) — Good Preference

Experts note that default VPN split-tunneling leaks real IP metadata and Google's behavioral algorithms map recurring Russian traffic patterns, shutting down access.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.17, +0.83) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Revelation.
Technical boundaries expose how behavioral telemetry overrides simple IP masking.

- Google Location Telemetry: PASS (0.2, -0.3) — Algorithmic tracking naturally identifies user jurisdiction beyond IP masks.
- VPN Split-Tunneling: PASS (-0.1, -0.2) — Default bypass settings leak direct connection metadata to services.

Google's Gemini AI has stopped working for some users in Russia, with outages flagged by Kod.ru and Downdetector. The disruption highlights how modern platforms use behavioral telemetry alongside IP addresses to determine user location.

The Bright Side:
It forces greater transparency regarding how tech platforms collect and utilize behavioral metadata across borders.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing IP-based access with behavioral telemetry. The physical reality of network routing overrides simple proxy tools.

Social Physics Analysis:
Platform telemetry aggregates user signals organically, creating friction when state-level blocks meet advanced geographic profiling without malicious intent from users.

The Trajectory: The Path of Revelation.
When you map the gap between stated access methods and actual telemetry enforcement, it plots a direct trajectory toward neutral stasis.

The Unavoidable Truth: Behavioral telemetry maps user location beyond simple IP masks.

The Unavoidable Lie: VPNs completely isolate user traffic from platform tracking by default.
